title: Avey-B
claim: Prior methods entangle similarity and weight terms in one step; ours separates them into distinct dynamic and static layers.
layout: 2 panels side-by-side, bottom-to-top graphs, red arrows linking nodes to equations
description: Two side-by-side panels compare parameterizations. Panel (a), labeled 'Avey's Coupled Parameterization', shows embeddings e1, e2, e3 at the bottom with arrows converging on a single cyan neuron n1. Each arrow is labeled with a product s·w, such as s11w11. A red curved arrow connects n1 to the equation n1 = s11w11e1 + s21w21e2 + s31w31e3. Panel (b), labeled 'Avey-B's Decoupled Parameterization', has the same embeddings feeding a cyan dynamic layer n(d) through arrows labeled s11, s21 and s31. A second, yellow static layer n(s) sits above it and is fed through arrows labeled w11, w21 and w31. Red arrows link nodes to two equations at the top. Faint gray edges show the connections to the other neurons. The eye goes first to the colored circles and the equations.
caption: A simple illustration of coupled (a) and decoupled (b) parameterizations (ei = embedding i; sij = cosine similarity score between ei and ej; ni = neuron i, ni(d) = neuron i in dynamic layer d; ni(s) = neuron i in static layer s; and wij = weight corresponding to ei or ni(d) used in the weighted sum of nj or nj(s), respectively).
abstract: Compact pretrained bidirectional encoders remain the backbone of industrial NLP under tight compute and memory budgets. Their effectiveness stems from self-attention's ability to deliver high-quality bidirectional contextualization with sequence-level parallelism, as popularized by BERT-style architectures. Recently, Avey was introduced as an autoregressive, attention-free alternative that naturally admits an encoder-only adaptation. In this paper, we reformulate Avey for the encoder-only paradigm and propose several innovations to its architecture, including decoupled static and dynamic parameterizations, stability-oriented normalization, and neural compression. Results show that this reformulated architecture compares favorably to four widely used Transformer-based encoders, consistently outperforming them on standard token-classification and information-retrieval benchmarks while scaling more efficiently to long contexts.
